title: "Atlas usage"
format:

    page-layout: full

How much the **public BrainGlobe atlas data** is being requested, derived from
the S3 server access logs of the atlas bucket. Only successful object
requests (`REST.GET.OBJECT`, HTTP 200/206) are counted. Totals are
cumulative since logging began and grow a little every day.

Each atlas is served as several resources — an annotation volume, one or more
reference/template images, a terminology, a packaged download, neuroglancer
state — under separate key namespaces. Only the annotation keys carry the
canonical atlas name, so the **per-atlas table and charts below count
annotation-set requests**; the other resource types are summarised together
under "by resource type".

The atlas, country and client-tool breakdowns are stored as three independent
tables (`atlas_usage.parquet`, `atlas_usage_by_country.parquet`,
`atlas_usage_by_tool.parquet`), so there is no per-atlas country or tool
split — the country and tool figures cover all requests.

The **client tool** is inferred from each request's `Referer` and
`User-Agent`: the browser viewers (neuroglancer, Pinpoint) set a recognisable
`Referer`; library/CLI clients are told apart by `User-Agent`, with
`aiobotocore`/`botocore` (i.e. `s3fs` + `zarr`) attributed to
`brainglobe-atlasapi`.

```{python}
# | label: load
from datetime import datetime
import json

import pandas as pd
from bokeh.io import output_notebook, show
from bokeh.layouts import column, gridplot
from bokeh.models import ColumnDataSource, CustomJS, Div, RadioButtonGroup
from bokeh.plotting import figure
from bokeh.resources import INLINE

from oss_dashboard.atlas_logs.atlas_names import display_name
from oss_dashboard.atlas_logs.constants import (
    ATLAS_PARQUET_PATH,
    COUNTRY_PARQUET_PATH,
    STATE_PATH,
    TOOL_PARQUET_PATH,
)

# Embeds BokehJS directly into the page rather than pointing at a CDN, so
# the charts also work fully offline.
output_notebook(resources=INLINE, hide_banner=True)

GREEN = "#03A062"
BLUE = "#4178f3"
ORANGE = "#EE9040"
PURPLE = "#7B61FF"
PINK = "#E0529C"
BROWN = "#B4622A"
# A mid grey that stays legible on both the light and dark site themes.
INK = "#888888"
GRID = "#88888840"


def _style(fig):
    """Transparent, theme-agnostic styling matching the site's light/dark toggle."""
    fig.background_fill_color = None
    fig.border_fill_color = None
    fig.outline_line_color = None
    fig.xgrid.grid_line_color = GRID
    fig.ygrid.grid_line_color = GRID
    fig.axis.axis_line_color = GRID
    fig.axis.major_tick_line_color = GRID
    fig.axis.minor_tick_line_color = None
    fig.axis.axis_label_text_color = INK
    fig.axis.major_label_text_color = INK
    if fig.title is not None:
        fig.title.text_color = INK
        fig.title.text_font_size = "13px"
    fig.toolbar.logo = None
    return fig


def _bar_figure(labels, keys, metrics, *, title, color):
    """A horizontal bar chart, largest value (in the first metric) at top,
    with a metric-toggle button group beneath it.

    ``metrics`` is ``[(key, button_label, unit_label, bar_values, daily_lookup,
    daily_total), ...]`` - the same short ``key`` used throughout to select
    which of several parallel value sets is currently shown. Only the bar
    chart's own lengths + axis label are wired here; call
    ``_wire_interactivity`` to also hook it up to a shared time series.
    """
    default_key, _, default_unit, default_values, _, _ = metrics[0]
    source = ColumnDataSource(
        data=dict(label=list(labels), key=list(keys), value=list(default_values))
    )
    fig = figure(
        y_range=list(labels),
        height=max(170, 26 * len(labels)) + (36 if len(metrics) > 1 else 0),
        sizing_mode="stretch_width",
        tools="tap,hover,reset",
        toolbar_location=None,
        title=title,
    )
    fig.hbar(
        y="label",
        right="value",
        height=0.7,
        source=source,
        fill_color=color,
        line_color=None,
        selection_fill_color=color,
        nonselection_fill_alpha=0.35,
    )
    fig.hover.tooltips = [("", "@label"), ("value", "@value{0,0.[00]}")]
    fig.xaxis.axis_label = default_unit
    fig.x_range.start = 0
    _style(fig)

    if len(metrics) > 1:
        selector = RadioButtonGroup(
            labels=[label for _, label, *_ in metrics], active=0
        )
    else:
        selector = None
    return fig, source, selector


def _wire_interactivity(fig, source, selector, metrics, prefix, *, ts_source, ts_fig, caption):
    """Wires a bar chart (built by ``_bar_figure``) to the shared time
    series: clicking a bar shows that entity's own daily trend in whichever
    metric the toggle is currently set to; clicking the same bar again, or
    switching metric, resets back to the overall total for that metric."""
    metric_keys = [m[0] for m in metrics]
    metric_labels = {m[0]: m[1] for m in metrics}
    units = {m[0]: m[2] for m in metrics}
    values_by_metric = {m[0]: m[3] for m in metrics}
    lookup_by_metric = {m[0]: m[4] for m in metrics}
    total_by_metric = {m[0]: m[5] for m in metrics}

    args = dict(
        bar_source=source,
        ts=ts_source,
        caption=caption,
        selector=selector,
        metric_keys=metric_keys,
        metric_labels=metric_labels,
        units=units,
        values_by_metric=values_by_metric,
        lookup_by_metric=lookup_by_metric,
        total_by_metric=total_by_metric,
        prefix=prefix,
        fig_xaxis=fig.xaxis[0],
        ts_yaxis=ts_fig.yaxis[0],
    )

    tap_callback = CustomJS(
        args=args,
        code="""
        const metric = selector ? metric_keys[selector.active] : metric_keys[0];
        const idx = cb_obj.indices;
        if (idx.length === 0) {
            ts.data['y'] = total_by_metric[metric];
            caption.text = 'Showing <b>all ' + metric_labels[metric] +
                '</b> &mdash; click a bar below to drill in';
        } else {
            const i = idx[idx.length - 1];
            const key = bar_source.data['key'][i];
            const series = (lookup_by_metric[metric] || {})[key];
            if (series !== undefined) {
                const label = bar_source.data['label'][i];
                ts.data['y'] = series;
                caption.text = 'Showing <b>' + prefix + ':</b> ' + label +
                    ' (' + metric_labels[metric] + ') &mdash; click the bar again to reset';
            }
        }
        ts.change.emit();
        ts_yaxis.axis_label = units[metric];
        """,
    )
    source.selected.js_on_change("indices", tap_callback)

    if selector is not None:
        metric_callback = CustomJS(
            args=args,
            code="""
            const metric = metric_keys[selector.active];
            bar_source.data['value'] = values_by_metric[metric];
            bar_source.change.emit();
            bar_source.selected.indices = [];
            fig_xaxis.axis_label = units[metric];
            ts.data['y'] = total_by_metric[metric];
            ts.change.emit();
            ts_yaxis.axis_label = units[metric];
            caption.text = 'Showing <b>all ' + metric_labels[metric] +
                '</b> &mdash; click a bar below to drill in';
            """,
        )
        selector.js_on_change("active", metric_callback)


GB = 1e9
TB = 1e12

def _read(path, columns):
    if path.exists():
        return pd.read_parquet(path)
    return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)


usage = _read(
    ATLAS_PARQUET_PATH,
    ["date", "atlas", "resource", "requests", "bytes_sent"],
)
countries = _read(
    COUNTRY_PARQUET_PATH,
    ["date", "country", "requests", "bytes_sent", "manifest_requests"],
)
tools = _read(
    TOOL_PARQUET_PATH,
    ["date", "tool", "requests", "bytes_sent", "manifest_requests"],
)
has_data = not usage.empty

state = json.loads(STATE_PATH.read_text()) if STATE_PATH.exists() else {}
updated_at = state.get("updated_at")
```

```{python}
# | label: no-data
# | output: asis
if not has_data:
    print(
        "::: callout-note\n"
        "No atlas usage data has been collected yet. Run "
        "`python -m oss_dashboard.atlas_logs` to populate "
        "`oss_dashboard/data/atlas_usage.parquet`.\n:::"

```

```{python}
# | label: derived
if has_data:
    usage["date"] = pd.to_datetime(usage["date"])
    countries["date"] = pd.to_datetime(countries["date"])

    # The per-atlas views use annotation-set requests only (see intro).
    annotations = usage[usage["resource"] == "annotation"]
    # The group-root zarr.json fetch for an annotation store - one per
    # "open", so a better popularity proxy than raw request counts (which
    # are skewed by array size and how much of it a client reads). Only
    # collected from the point this classification was added; see the note
    # by the table below.
    annotation_manifests = usage[usage["resource"] == "annotation-manifest"]

    by_atlas = (
        annotations.groupby("atlas")
        .agg(
            requests=("requests", "sum"),
            gb=("bytes_sent", lambda s: s.sum() / GB),
        )
        .sort_values("requests", ascending=False)
    )
    by_atlas["manifest_opens"] = (
        annotation_manifests.groupby("atlas")["requests"]
        .sum()
        .reindex(by_atlas.index, fill_value=0)
        .astype(int)
    )
    # Human-readable name for display; the index stays the raw key derived
    # by classify_key (used to filter "unclassified" etc).
    by_atlas["name"] = [display_name(atlas) for atlas in by_atlas.index]

    by_country = (
        countries.groupby("country")["requests"]
        .sum()
        .sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    by_country_gb = countries.groupby("country")["bytes_sent"].sum() / GB
    by_resource = (
        usage.groupby("resource")["requests"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    by_resource_gb = usage.groupby("resource")["bytes_sent"].sum() / GB
    by_tool = (
        tools.groupby("tool")["requests"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    tool_gb = tools.groupby("tool")["bytes_sent"].sum() / GB
    by_day = (
        usage.groupby("date")
        .agg(requests=("requests", "sum"), bytes_sent=("bytes_sent", "sum"))
        .asfreq("D", fill_value=0)
    )
    if not tools.empty:
        tools["date"] = pd.to_datetime(tools["date"])
        # Reindexed onto the same daily index as every other breakdown
        # below, so all the drilldown series line up on one shared axis.
        tool_daily = (
            tools.pivot_table(
                index="date", columns="tool", values="requests",
                aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0,
            )
            .reindex(by_day.index, fill_value=0)
            .reindex(columns=by_tool.index)
        )
        tool_bytes_daily = (
            tools.pivot_table(
                index="date", columns="tool", values="bytes_sent",
                aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0,
            )
            .reindex(by_day.index, fill_value=0)
            .reindex(columns=by_tool.index)
        )
    else:
        tool_daily = pd.DataFrame(index=by_day.index)
        tool_bytes_daily = pd.DataFrame(index=by_day.index)

    total_requests = int(usage["requests"].sum())
    total_bytes = int(usage["bytes_sent"].sum())
    annotation_requests = int(annotations["requests"].sum())
    n_atlases = int((by_atlas.index != "unclassified").sum())
    n_countries = int((by_country.index != "??").sum())
    span = f"{by_day.index.min():%d %b %Y} – {by_day.index.max():%d %b %Y}"
    n_days = by_day.shape[0]
    country_total = int(by_country.sum())
    unresolved_countries = int(by_country.get("??", 0))

    # {group value -> [value per day]}, aligned to by_day.index, used to
    # drive the click-to-drilldown time series below - all computed once
    # here so the interactive charts are pure client-side JS afterwards.
    def _daily_lookup(df, group_col, value_col):
        if df.empty:
            return {}
        pivot = (
            df.groupby(["date", group_col])[value_col]
            .sum()
            .unstack(fill_value=0)
            .reindex(by_day.index, fill_value=0)
        )
        return {str(col): pivot[col].tolist() for col in pivot.columns}

    def _gb(d):
        return {k: [round(v / GB, 3) for v in vs] for k, vs in d.items()}

    atlas_daily = _daily_lookup(annotations, "atlas", "requests")
    atlas_manifest_daily = _daily_lookup(annotation_manifests, "atlas", "requests")
    atlas_gb_daily = _gb(_daily_lookup(annotations, "atlas", "bytes_sent"))

    resource_daily = _daily_lookup(usage, "resource", "requests")
    resource_gb_daily = _gb(_daily_lookup(usage, "resource", "bytes_sent"))

    country_daily = _daily_lookup(countries, "country", "requests")
    country_gb_daily = _gb(_daily_lookup(countries, "country", "bytes_sent"))
    # Country/tool have no resource dimension, so "manifest opens" here means
    # *any* resource type's group-root zarr.json (annotation, template, ...)
    # - broader than the atlas chart's annotation-only manifest opens.
    country_manifest_daily = _daily_lookup(countries, "country", "manifest_requests")
    by_country_manifest = countries.groupby("country")["manifest_requests"].sum()

    tool_daily_lookup = {
        str(col): tool_daily[col].fillna(0).astype(int).tolist()
        for col in tool_daily.columns
    }
    tool_gb_daily_lookup = {
        str(col): [round(v / GB, 3) for v in tool_bytes_daily[col].fillna(0).tolist()]
        for col in tool_bytes_daily.columns
    }
    tool_manifest_daily = _daily_lookup(tools, "tool", "manifest_requests")
    by_tool_manifest = tools.groupby("tool")["manifest_requests"].sum()

    total_daily = by_day["requests"].astype(int).tolist()
    total_gb_daily = [round(v / GB, 3) for v in by_day["bytes_sent"].tolist()]
    total_manifest_daily = (
        annotation_manifests.groupby("date")["requests"]
        .sum()
        .reindex(by_day.index, fill_value=0)
        .astype(int)
        .tolist()
    )
    total_manifest_all_daily = (
        countries.groupby("date")["manifest_requests"]
        .sum()
        .reindex(by_day.index, fill_value=0)
        .astype(int)
        .tolist()
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: stat-cards
# | output: asis
if has_data:
    cards = [
        ("Requests", f"{total_requests:,}"),
        ("Data served", f"{total_bytes / TB:.2f} TB"),
        ("Atlases", f"{n_atlases}"),
        ("Annotation requests", f"{annotation_requests:,}"),
        ("Countries", f"{n_countries}"),
        ("Days covered", f"{n_days}"),
        ("Window", span),
    ]
    if not by_tool.empty:
        share = by_tool.iloc[0] / by_tool.sum() * 100
        cards.insert(
            4, ("Top client", f"{by_tool.index[0]} ({share:.0f}%)")
        )
    tiles = "".join(
        f'<div style="flex:1 1 8rem;border:1px solid {INK}55;border-radius:.5rem;'
        f'padding:.75rem 1rem">'
        f'<div style="font-size:.8rem;color:{INK}">{label}</div>'
        f'<div style="font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:600">{value}</div></div>'
        for label, value in cards
    )
    print(
        f'<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.75rem;margin:1rem 0">'
        f"{tiles}</div>"
    )
    if updated_at:
        stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(updated_at).strftime(
            "%A, %d %B %Y %H:%M UTC"
        )
        print(f"\n*Data last updated: {stamp}*\n")
```

## Requests by atlas

**Manifest opens** counts only the one metadata fetch (`zarr.json`) a client
makes when it *opens* an atlas's annotation store, not the many
resolution/chunk files it then reads - so unlike raw request counts, it
isn't skewed by array size or how much of the array a given client actually
pulls, making it the closer proxy for "how many times has this atlas been
downloaded." Sort by that column instead of "Requests" for a popularity
ranking; it's also selectable as a metric on the atlas chart below.

```{python}
# | label: table
if has_data:
    import itables

    table = by_atlas.reset_index()[["name", "requests", "manifest_opens", "gb"]]
    table.columns = ["Atlas", "Requests", "Manifest opens", "Data served (GB)"]
    table["Data served (GB)"] = table["Data served (GB)"].round(1)
    table["Share of requests"] = (
        table["Requests"] / annotation_requests * 100
    ).round(1).astype(str) + "%"
    itables.show(
        table,
        classes="display nowrap cell-border",
        columnDefs=[{"className": "dt-left", "targets": "_all"}],
        order=[[1, "desc"]],
        paging=False,
        scrollX=True,
    )
```

## Explore interactively

Each chart below can switch between **requests**, **manifest opens** and
**data served** with the buttons underneath it - except "by resource type",
where manifest opens are already broken out as their own rows (e.g.
`annotation-manifest`), so a toggle for it would be redundant. Note that
"manifest opens" means something slightly narrower for atlas specifically -
only its annotation store's opens (the popularity proxy from the note
above) - versus country/tool, where it covers a store opening of *any*
resource type, since those breakdowns don't carry a resource dimension to
narrow it further. Click a bar to see *that slice's own* daily
trend, in whichever metric is selected, in the time series above; click the
bar again, or switch metric, to reset back to the overall total.

```{python}
# | label: explorer
if has_data:
    caption = Div(
        text="Showing <b>all requests</b> &mdash; click a bar below to drill in",
        styles={"color": INK, "font-size": "0.85rem"},
    )

    ts_source = ColumnDataSource(data=dict(x=list(by_day.index), y=total_daily))
    ts_fig = figure(
        x_axis_type="datetime",
        height=260,
        sizing_mode="stretch_width",
        tools="hover,reset,xpan,xwheel_zoom",
        toolbar_location="above",
        title="Over time",
    )
    ts_fig.line("x", "y", source=ts_source, color=GREEN, line_width=2)
    ts_fig.hover.tooltips = [("date", "@x{%F}"), ("value", "@y{0,0.[00]}")]
    ts_fig.hover.formatters = {"@x": "datetime"}
    ts_fig.hover.mode = "vline"
    ts_fig.yaxis.axis_label = "requests / day"
    ts_fig.y_range.start = 0
    _style(ts_fig)

    def _panel(fig, source, selector):
        return column(fig, selector, sizing_mode="stretch_width") if selector else fig

    top_atlas = (
        by_atlas[by_atlas.index != "unclassified"].head(15).sort_values("requests")
    )
    atlas_metrics = [
        ("requests", "Requests", "requests / day",
         top_atlas["requests"].tolist(), atlas_daily, total_daily),
        ("manifest", "Manifest opens", "manifest opens / day",
         top_atlas["manifest_opens"].tolist(), atlas_manifest_daily, total_manifest_daily),
        ("gb", "GB served", "GB / day",
         top_atlas["gb"].round(2).tolist(), atlas_gb_daily, total_gb_daily),
    ]
    atlas_fig, atlas_source, atlas_selector = _bar_figure(
        [display_name(k) for k in top_atlas.index],
        list(top_atlas.index),
        atlas_metrics,
        title="By atlas (top 15)",
        color=GREEN,
    )
    _wire_interactivity(
        atlas_fig, atlas_source, atlas_selector, atlas_metrics, "atlas",
        ts_source=ts_source, ts_fig=ts_fig, caption=caption,
    )

    top_country = by_country[by_country.index != "??"].head(15).sort_values()
    country_metrics = [
        ("requests", "Requests", "requests / day",
         top_country.tolist(), country_daily, total_daily),
        ("manifest", "Manifest opens", "manifest opens / day",
         by_country_manifest.reindex(top_country.index, fill_value=0).tolist(),
         country_manifest_daily, total_manifest_all_daily),
        ("gb", "GB served", "GB / day",
         by_country_gb.reindex(top_country.index, fill_value=0).round(2).tolist(),
         country_gb_daily, total_gb_daily),
    ]
    country_fig, country_source, country_selector = _bar_figure(
        list(top_country.index), list(top_country.index), country_metrics,
        title="By country (top 15)",
        color=ORANGE,
    )
    _wire_interactivity(
        country_fig, country_source, country_selector, country_metrics, "country",
        ts_source=ts_source, ts_fig=ts_fig, caption=caption,
    )

    resource_sorted = by_resource.sort_values()
    resource_metrics = [
        ("requests", "Requests", "requests / day",
         resource_sorted.tolist(), resource_daily, total_daily),
        ("gb", "GB served", "GB / day",
         by_resource_gb.reindex(resource_sorted.index, fill_value=0).round(2).tolist(),
         resource_gb_daily, total_gb_daily),
    ]
    resource_fig, resource_source, resource_selector = _bar_figure(
        list(resource_sorted.index), list(resource_sorted.index), resource_metrics,
        title="By resource type",
        color=PURPLE,
    )
    _wire_interactivity(
        resource_fig, resource_source, resource_selector, resource_metrics, "resource type",
        ts_source=ts_source, ts_fig=ts_fig, caption=caption,
    )

    tool_sorted = by_tool.sort_values()
    tool_metrics = [
        ("requests", "Requests", "requests / day",
         tool_sorted.tolist(), tool_daily_lookup, total_daily),
        ("manifest", "Manifest opens", "manifest opens / day",
         by_tool_manifest.reindex(tool_sorted.index, fill_value=0).tolist(),
         tool_manifest_daily, total_manifest_all_daily),
        ("gb", "GB served", "GB / day",
         tool_gb.reindex(tool_sorted.index, fill_value=0).round(2).tolist(),
         tool_gb_daily_lookup, total_gb_daily),
    ]
    tool_fig, tool_source, tool_selector = _bar_figure(
        list(tool_sorted.index), list(tool_sorted.index), tool_metrics,
        title="By client tool",
        color=BLUE,
    )
    _wire_interactivity(
        tool_fig, tool_source, tool_selector, tool_metrics, "client tool",
        ts_source=ts_source, ts_fig=ts_fig, caption=caption,
    )

    grid = gridplot(
        [
            [_panel(atlas_fig, atlas_source, atlas_selector),
             _panel(country_fig, country_source, country_selector)],
            [_panel(resource_fig, resource_source, resource_selector),
             _panel(tool_fig, tool_source, tool_selector)],
        ],
        sizing_mode="stretch_width",
        toolbar_location=None,
    )
    show(column(caption, ts_fig, grid, sizing_mode="stretch_width"))
```

## Per day by client tool

```{python}
# | label: tool-over-time
if has_data and not tool_daily.empty and tool_daily.shape[0] > 1:
    top_cols = list(tool_daily.sum().sort_values(ascending=False).index[:6])
    # Fixed hue order, checked with the design system's CVD-separation
    # validator (adjacent pairs pass in this order); a plain grey read as
    # colourless and failed, hence BROWN as the 6th hue instead of INK.
    palette = [GREEN, BLUE, ORANGE, PURPLE, PINK, BROWN]

    fig = figure(
        x_axis_type="datetime",
        height=380,
        sizing_mode="stretch_width",
        tools="hover,reset,xpan,xwheel_zoom",
        toolbar_location="above",
        title="Per day by client tool (top 6) — click a legend entry to isolate it",
    )
    dates = list(tool_daily.index)
    line_sources = []
    for name, color in zip(top_cols, palette):
        src = ColumnDataSource(data=dict(
            x=dates,
            y=tool_daily[name].tolist(),
            y_requests=tool_daily[name].tolist(),
            y_manifest=tool_manifest_daily.get(str(name), [0] * len(dates)),
            y_gb=[round(v / GB, 3) for v in tool_bytes_daily[name].tolist()],
        ))
        line_sources.append(src)
        fig.line(
            "x", "y", source=src, color=color, line_width=2,
            legend_label=str(name), name=str(name),
        )
    fig.legend.click_policy = "hide"
    fig.legend.location = "top_left"
    fig.legend.background_fill_alpha = 0
    fig.legend.border_line_alpha = 0
    fig.legend.label_text_color = INK
    fig.y_range.start = 0
    fig.yaxis.axis_label = "requests / day"
    fig.hover.tooltips = [("tool", "$name"), ("date", "@x{%F}"), ("value", "@y{0,0.[00]}")]
    fig.hover.formatters = {"@x": "datetime"}
    fig.hover.mode = "vline"
    _style(fig)

    tool_selector = RadioButtonGroup(
        labels=["Requests", "Manifest opens", "GB served"], active=0
    )
    tool_selector.js_on_change("active", CustomJS(
        args=dict(sources=line_sources, fig_yaxis=fig.yaxis[0]),
        code="""
        const keys = ['y_requests', 'y_manifest', 'y_gb'];
        const labels = ['requests / day', 'manifest opens / day', 'GB / day'];
        const key = keys[cb_obj.active];
        for (const src of sources) {
            src.data['y'] = src.data[key];
            src.change.emit();
        }
        fig_yaxis.axis_label = labels[cb_obj.active];
        """,
    ))
    show(column(fig, tool_selector, sizing_mode="stretch_width"))
```

## Client tool breakdown

```{python}
# | label: tool-table
# | output: asis
if has_data and not by_tool.empty:
    total = by_tool.sum()
    lines = ["| Client tool | Requests | Share | Data served (GB) |",
             "| --- | --: | --: | --: |"]
    for name, requests in by_tool.items():
        lines.append(
            f"| {name} | {requests:,} | {requests / total * 100:.1f}% "
            f"| {tool_gb.get(name, 0):,.1f} |"
        )
    print("\n".join(lines))
```
